operations.helperRationale: One call instead of the agent hand-paging timesheets or string-matching timestamps: { id } (or a bare number) is a direct get, { begin } (or a bare timestamp) is one bounded server-filtered read (begin&user=all, a single 500-record page — the vendor supplies the filter, so no client scan and no RESOLUTION_TRUNCATED); a unique hit returns the compact TimesheetSummary, zero hits null, more than one throws RESOLUTION_AMBIGUOUS with the candidate ids.

metadata.purpose: Resolve one timesheet from an id or a begin timestamp.
metadata.usage: Accepts { id }, { begin } or a bare numeric id / begin timestamp; timesheets have no name field, so any other text resolves to nothing. The begin filter is "at or after", so a stale timestamp matches many records and throws RESOLUTION_AMBIGUOUS — narrow it. A miss by id throws NOT_FOUND (never null). No client scan occurs (vendor filter), so the scan never truncates. expand: true for the full record; resolutionDetails: true for the Resolution wrapper (cost, scanned, scanTruncated).
metadata.preferredWhen: Preferred over timesheets.list for any identifier lookup — it removes the paging and the hand-matching.

tests.title: returns the compact TimesheetSummary for a unique begin filter
returns null when the begin filter matches no timesheet
throws RESOLUTION_AMBIGUOUS with the candidate ids when begin matches several timesheets
throws NOT_FOUND when the id does not exist
returns the Resolution wrapper (resolutionCost, scanned, scanTruncated) for resolutionDetails: true
returns the full record for expand: true
ResolutionError.truncated emits RESOLUTION_TRUNCATED (category resolution, not retryable)

operations.helperRationale: One bounded server-side read instead of a page walk: passes every spec filter (user/users/customer/customers/project/projects/activity/activities/tags/orderBy/order/begin/end/exported/active/billable/full/modified_after/term) unchanged, enforces an explicit limit (default 25, hard max 100 — garbage throws KimaiConfigError, never a silent clamp), defaults to user=all, and returns compact TimesheetSummary rows with an expand escape hatch.

metadata.purpose: Search timesheets with the spec filters, bounded by an explicit limit.
metadata.usage: limit defaults to 25, hard max 100 (a non-integer or out-of-range value throws KimaiConfigError — never silently clamped). Without a user filter the SDK passes user=all (requires the vendor view_other_timesheet permission). Compact TimesheetSummary rows by default; expand: true for the full records.
metadata.preferredWhen: Preferred over timesheets.list for any bounded filtered read (at most 100 rows).

tests.title: returns compact TimesheetSummary rows for the spec filters

sends size 25 when no limit is given
sends size 100 when limit is 100
throws KimaiConfigError for a limit above 100 or a non-integer limit
returns the full records for expand: true

operations.helperRationale: The approved workflow resource (timesheets) bundles the timesheet with its referenced user, activity, project and customer in a bounded pool (at most three in flight, then the dependent customer read) — without it the agent chains four or five gets and reasons through the references itself.

metadata.purpose: Fetch a timesheet with its referenced user, activity, project and customer.
metadata.usage: user and activity are null when the record carries no reference; project is null when absent; customer is null unless the project carries one. Compact TimesheetSummary by default; expand: true for the full timesheet record.
metadata.preferredWhen: Preferred over get + individual user/activity/project/customer reads: one call instead of four or five.

tests.title: returns the timesheet with its referenced user, activity, project and customer

operations.helperRationale: Two paths, both bounded: { id } fetches directly (server-side); a username has no vendor filter, so it is matched exactly over a bounded client scan of the user list (cap 500 records; the vendor users collection is unpaginated, so the record cap is the effective bound). A miss after a complete scan returns null; a truncated scan throws RESOLUTION_TRUNCATED (never null); several exact matches throw RESOLUTION_AMBIGUOUS.

metadata.purpose: Resolve one user from an identifier.
metadata.usage: Accepts { id }, { username } or a bare numeric id / exact username. The username path scans the user list with a bounded cap (cap 500 records; the collection is unpaginated); a truncated scan throws RESOLUTION_TRUNCATED and an ambiguous match throws RESOLUTION_AMBIGUOUS with the candidate ids.
metadata.preferredWhen: Preferred over users.list + a client-side find for any single-user lookup.
